topics.label: Course introduction and lecture learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series and outlines the core learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Biological basis of cancer and tissue architecture failure
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the fundamental nature of cancer as a breakdown of normal cellular differentiation and tissue architecture driven by accumulated genetic and epigenetic changes.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and malignant progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how invasion and metastasis distinguish malignant from benign tumors and illustrate the stepwise pathological progression of neoplastic lesions.

topics.label: Conventions and exceptions in tumor nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard rules and pathological exceptions used to name and classify benign and malignant neoplasms across different tissue lineages.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer-induced morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the mechanical, metabolic, and physiological processes through which primary tumors and distant metastases cause severe illness and death.

topics.label: Comparative cancer incidence across humans and other animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyse the epidemiological patterns of tumor frequency across human populations and examine cancer incidence across diverse multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Principles and efficacy of clinical cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the diagnostic rationale, histological detection methods, and clinical limitations associated with population-level cancer screening programs.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the session by reviewing the learning outcomes and providing logistical instructions for upcoming practicals.
